### 3. Systemic ffmpeg-spawn guard gap — flagged, NOT yet fixed, needs a real sweep

Found while chasing a live crash report (video open + storyboard
build racing). Fixed the one confirmed live site
(`gui/src/helpers/video/storyboard.py`, commit `d4b10243`) but a
broader search found **17 other files** spawning ffmpeg/ffprobe
without the same `media_backend_spawn_guard()` protection (issue #81
crash family — first `QMediaPlayer` construction lazily dlopens Qt
Multimedia's native backend; a concurrent ffmpeg fork with the JVM
loaded in-process aborts the process). List is in the bus post
`.agent/bus/2026-08-18.md`, "swarm-prep landed; found + fixed the live
QSocketNotifier crash..." — includes `video_extractor_worker.py`,
`gif_extractor_worker.py`, `frame_extractor_worker.py`,
`sampler_worker.py`, `queue_execution_worker.py`, `_qml_handlers.py`,
`frame_selection_dialog.py`, and others. Fix pattern is mechanical
(wrap the fork in `media_backend_spawn_guard()` from
`gui.src.helpers.video.video_thumbnailer`) but each site needs a
judgment call: guard the whole call (`subprocess.run`) or just the
fork (`Popen`, if a long streaming read follows — see the storyboard.py
fix for the pattern). **Nobody has claimed this yet.**

### 4. ASP rendering test suite doesn't collect — flagged, unconfirmed

`backend/test/conftest.py`'s manual package load hits a circular-
import-shaped `ModuleNotFoundError` in a completely clean environment
(confirmed via `git stash` to `f549ec1`, opencode's own last known-good
commit). Tried multiple invocations (parent venv, `uv run` from
`backend/`, from ASP root, clean env) — same failure every time. Asked
opencode on the bus to confirm whether `uv run pytest
backend/test/rendering/ -q` still passes for them. **Check the bus for
their answer** — if it doesn't reproduce for them, there's an
environment difference worth finding; if it does, this is a real,
currently-blocking regression on top of #427's landing.

## Environment notes for this machine

- Ubuntu, KDE Plasma/Wayland, NVIDIA RTX 3090 Ti (proprietary driver,
  kernel/userspace version mismatch — a reboot may fix native Wayland
  without needing `GDK_BACKEND=x11`).
- Snap-confined launching terminal — `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`/`GIO_MODULE_DIR`
  etc. leak into GUI subprocesses; clear them when launching Tauri/Qt
  apps from a snap-confined shell (see `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`).
- `IMAGE_TOOLKIT_TELEMETRY=1` measurably perturbs timing enough to
  mask the gallery-scan race — don't rely on it to reproduce that
  specific crash class.
